body:
Adds a `predge` plugin with one action, **Read Predge Signal**, that fetches a wallet's smart-money conviction signal from Predge, verifies it offline, and checks its shape before the step succeeds.

## What it does
- `GET {PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL}/v1/signal/:wallet` (default `https://api.predge.io`, free, unauthenticated) through `safeFetch` behind an always-on `assertUrlIsPublic` SSRF check, with a 10s `AbortSignal.timeout` and a 64 KiB cap on the body, checked against `content-length` before it is read and against the body length before it is parsed.
- Verifies the detached ed25519 attestation offline with WebCrypto — the thing a Code node cannot do, since its sandbox exposes `crypto` as `{ randomUUID }` with no `subtle`. Six ordered checks: scheme; **signer pinned to Predge's published key** (default is a source constant, `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` overrides it, and the key the response carries is never trusted on its own); ed25519 signature over the canonical payload; **subject binding** to the requested wallet; **`resource` binding** to `conviction:<wallet>`, so a different signed product about the same wallet under the same key is not read as a conviction signal; and **freshness** (`issuedAt` within a max-age window, default 600s, `PREDGE_MAX_SIGNAL_AGE_SECONDS` to tune, one minute of skew tolerance).
- **Then checks the payload shape.** A signature establishes who issued the bytes and that they did not change, not what is in them. Every field the step returns is checked before success: `conviction` a finite number in 0-100 (a numeric string is a failure, not a number — `"99999" >= 80` coerces true in a template gate), `action` one of `accumulate`/`reduce`/`hold`, `window` one of `7d`/`30d`, each required. Nothing is coerced.
- **The step fails on either gate**, with the reason, or the field and its received and expected types, in its error — so a successful step is a verified signal whose fields are the documented shape, and there is no `verified` flag to forget to gate on. Success outputs: `wallet`, `conviction`, `action`, `window`, `signer`, `issuedAt`, `ageSeconds`.
- Error attribution, not retry behaviour: a 429 and a 5xx are `EXTERNAL`; a 404, a 402 and an unparseable `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL` are `USER`; a body that is not a Predge response is `EXTERNAL` unless the operator repointed the host.

## Trust model
The default pin is a source constant in `predge-core.ts`, equal to the `attestation`-role key published at `https://api.predge.io/.well-known/predge-keys.json`. Nothing reads the keyset at run time — that would let the response pick its own key with an extra hop. Rotation is therefore a plugin release; `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` lets an operator move ahead of one, as noted in `credentials.ts`.

## Tests
`tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts` drives the WebCrypto path: a captured live 200 verifying against the default pin with no override (so the constant is exercised against Predge's real bytes), pinned pass, responder-chooses-its-own-key, wrong signer, tampered payload, wrong wallet, stale, future, case-insensitive match, malformed bodies, and the step failing closed. On top of that: the four payload-shape reproductions from review, each run against the real step with a correctly signed envelope; both ends of the conviction range accepted; a `track-record:` envelope and a `conviction:` resource naming a different wallet rejected; and every non-200 branch of `fetchSignedSignal` — 404, 402, 429, 5xx, unexpected 4xx, non-JSON, oversized by header and by body, SSRF, unparseable URL.

`pnpm check`, `pnpm type-check` and the unit suite are clean at head. Rebased onto `staging`; `lib/types/integration.ts` and the rest of the generated files are a `pnpm discover-plugins` run, not hand edits.

Closes #2482

This pull request comes from a fork, so GitHub does not pass it the credentials `build` normally uses for our image registry cache and staging build configuration. The build still runs and still compiles the image, so a red `build` here is real; it just takes longer than on team branches.

Every workflow run on a pull request from a fork also waits for a maintainer to approve it, so checks can sit at "awaiting approval" for a while after each push. Nothing is needed from you for either of these.

Thanks — this is the kind of review that makes the code better. Pushed `88ac779` addressing it.

**The blocking one — a failed verification no longer returns `success: true`.** `read-signal.ts` now fails the step with `{ success: false, error: "Predge signal did not verify: <reason>", errorClass: EXTERNAL }` when `verified` is false, and reads `signed.attestation.payload` only after that check. That closes all four you traced off that line: the `200 {}` TypeError (the malformed case now returns `verified: false` from `verifyPredgeSignal` before any dereference), the wallet reported under the wrong wallet (`wallet` is now the requested address, reached only after subject binding held), and the `subjectMatch: true` on pre-signature paths — `verifyPredgeSignal` now reports `subjectMatch: true` only after scheme, signer and signature hold, and `false` on every early return.

**Malformed / non-string fields.** The malformed guard runs first and type-checks `scheme`, `keyId` and `payload.wallet` before any string method touches them, so `{"wallet": 123}` or a numeric `keyId` from a self-hosted URL returns a clean `verified: false` / `malformed attestation` instead of throwing.

**keyId vs kid — with a live fixture.** You're right that nothing exercised the default constant against real bytes. It does now: the test carries a captured live 200 and asserts it verifies against `DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER` with **no** override. The attestation's `keyId` is the 64-hex `public_key`, not the 16-hex `kid`, so the constant matches what the service emits and the test fails if that drifts.

**Live wallet.** Your 404s were the example placeholder — the old one was a token address, not a tracked wallet. Three that carry a signal right now:
- `0x0224bb9eb0a5c9fd261ac9123a72cbdd5748292a`
- `0x19f15790253485a8a34306d946954e7c6cddf301`
- `0x0bf774022f0bd6ea21b587e793306a8f2ee60fb8`

The plugin's example wallet is now `0x0224…292a`, so it returns a live 200 out of the box. Only verified smart-money wallets carry a signal; everything else is a 404 by design.

**The rest.** `parseMaxAgeSeconds` honors `0`; `ageSeconds` is documented as possibly negative and the `-1` sentinel is gone from the success path; `signer` now says "verified against"; a rotation note sits next to `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` in `credentials.ts`; `lib/types/integration.ts` is regenerated with `pnpm discover-plugins` so the header and the union agree; and the PR body is rewritten. Running `tsgo --noEmit` also surfaced a latent `Uint8Array` → `BufferSource` type error in the WebCrypto path that predated this review — fixed. 14/14 unit tests pass.

On the allowlist / root-of-trust question: that's the right one to take to the team, and I'm not asking to shortcut it. If a per-org or beta dimension is where it lands, I'm glad to wire the plugin to whatever shape that takes.

Pushed. Branch is `b9575946` on top of `13d7f31c1`.

## The four

`predge-core.ts:89-103` — both doc comments rewritten. `verified` now says it is internal and why the step fails instead of returning it: a workflow that reads a boolean can forget to branch on it. `subjectMatch` now says false means "not established" rather than "mismatch", since failure paths that never compared the wallets report it too.

`index.ts:62` — help text says 0 is taken literally and rejects everything, and points at "a few seconds" as the strictest usable value. I did not floor it. Flooring would quietly give an operator something other than what they typed, which is the behaviour the literal-0 change was correcting.

`read-signal.ts:97` — this is the one place I went further than you asked, and I would rather flag it than have you find it.

You named two reasons as operator-caused. I only class them that way when the operator actually configured the thing in question. A pinned-key mismatch is a typo when they supplied `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID`, but on the default pin it is us rotating a key, which is ours to own. A malformed body is their parsing problem when they repointed `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL`, but on the default host it is us serving garbage. So the classifier reads the credentials, and the same two reasons stay `EXTERNAL` when nothing was set. Four tests pin both halves of each, 14 to 18.

If you would rather have the flat version, say so and I will flatten it.

## Rebase

Done, and one thing worth knowing for the next plugin. Resolving `plugin-allowlist.json` in staging's favour and re-running `discover-plugins` does not restore the plugin, because that file is the generator's input, not its output. It silently produced a registry without predge. I added the entry back and regenerated, and the three generated files now agree. Worth a line in the contributor docs if plugin PRs routinely hit this.

## The root of trust

Take your time on it. While you do, let me put the distinction where you can argue with it, since you were right that it belongs in the thread.

The pin does not ask KeeperHub to believe Predge's judgment. It asks it to believe that a given byte string left Predge unaltered. A workflow author who reads a held signature as "the conviction score is correct" has made an error, and the plugin should not help them make it. That is most of why `verified` is no longer an output.

What the pin replaces is worse than what it introduces. Without it the verifier trusts whatever key the response carries, which is to say it trusts the transport and verifies nothing. The pin removes that, and its failure mode is loud and closed: a rotation breaks every default-configured gate until a release ships the new constant, which is the direction you want a trust failure to fail.

On precedent, I would frame the question narrower than "may a plugin pin a third party". It is "may a plugin ship a constant that makes its own provenance claims checkable offline". The alternative for every future external-data plugin is unsigned data and a comment asking the operator to trust the vendor's TLS.

And a concession, if shipping someone else's key in the repo is the sticking point rather than pinning as such: make `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` required and drop `DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER` entirely. The operator then pins the key themselves from our well-known path, the repo carries no third-party key material, and the precedent you set is only that a plugin may verify against an operator-supplied key. It costs onboarding friction and it removes your objection completely. I am happy to do it that way. Tell me which you prefer before I write it.

One more thing on the live fixture: thank you for checking it against `/.well-known/predge-keys.json` rather than taking it on trust. That is the review I would have wanted and did not expect.

Both mechanical items are already on the branch. `85b6888d1` corrects the `PredgeVerifyResult` doc comments in `predge-core.ts` and rewrites the `maxSignalAgeSeconds` help text in `index.ts` to state that `0` is taken literally and rejects everything, since any network round trip already exceeds it. It landed at 09:28 UTC today, about two hours after your review at 07:36 UTC, so the increment you read was `035629b` rather than head. Head is `b9575946e`, and the commit after it is only the regenerated registry from the rebase onto staging.

On the correlated failures you are right, and it is the sharper version of the point I conceded. `EXTERNAL` resolving to `code: null` means a rotation is loud in every affected run record and quiet to anyone on call, and because the default pin is a source constant, one bad rotation is every default-configured gate failing at once rather than one workflow. That is a property of pinning rather than something the plugin can classify its way out of. `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` is the per-operator escape and the help text now names it, but it gives an operator no advance warning. The honest fix is on our side: publish the next key before we cut over rather than at cutover, so an operator can pin ahead of a rotation. If that would settle the concern I will write it into the keyset docs as a commitment with a stated notice period.

On the guaranteed live wallet, agreed, no second route. I will name `0x0224bb9eb0a5c9fd261ac9123a72cbdd5748292a` in the plugin docs as a currently-signalled address, with the caveat that it is a live wallet rather than a fixture, so what is promised is that it is signalling today and not that it will forever.

And noted on the UNI contract address. That round trip was worth it.

All three blocking items and the seven mechanical ones are in `62edf7b`, pushed on a rebase onto `staging`. Point by point.

## Blocking

**Payload shape.** You are right, and the four reproductions were reproducible here. The signature established who issued the bytes and that they had not changed; nothing established what was in them, and `conviction`, `action` and `window` went straight from the verified payload into the step's typed output.

`parseConvictionPayload` (`predge-core.ts`) now runs after verification and before success, and checks every field the step exposes: `conviction` a finite `number` in 0-100, `action` one of `accumulate`/`reduce`/`hold`, `window` one of `7d`/`30d`, each required. Nothing is coerced, so a numeric string is a failure and not a number — `"99999" >= 80` is exactly why. A failure fails the step with the field, what arrived and what was expected:

```
conviction: "99999"  -> Predge signal payload is not a conviction signal:
                        conviction must be a finite number in 0-100, got string "99999"
conviction: absent   -> conviction must be a finite number in 0-100, got missing
action: {"evil":1}   -> action must be one of accumulate, reduce, hold, got object
conviction: -500     -> conviction must be in 0-100, got number -500
```

Each of the four is a test against the real step with the real verifier and a correctly signed envelope, asserting `success: false` and that the field is named; `window: "90d"`, `action: "liquidate"`, `conviction: 101` and `conviction: null` are there too, and 0 and 100 are asserted to pass. I checked the tests fail without the fix rather than trusting that they pass with it: stubbing the check out fails 9 of them, and nothing else.

**`resource`.** Also right, and this is the better of the two fixes because it closes the absent-field case a layer earlier. `verifyPredgeSignal` now compares `resource` against `conviction:<requested wallet>` on the same signed bytes, immediately after the subject binding:

```
attestation is for "track-record:0x…", expected "conviction:0x…"
```

Two tests cover it: a same-key, same-scheme, same-wallet envelope carrying `conviction_score` and `verdict`, and a `conviction:` resource naming a different wallet. Same mutation check — removing the comparison fails both and nothing else.

One correction on the mechanism, since it affects how much the field is load-bearing rather than whether the fix is right. The wallet track-record route does not emit this envelope today: it uses the `version`/`issuer`/`public_key`/`canonical`/`payload` shape from the shared signer, with no `scheme` field, so it would not reach the payload checks. `/v1/signal/` is the only route emitting `veri402-ed25519-v1`. What holds is your actual point: the same key signs both families, `scheme` is a constant any issuer can stamp, and nothing in the plugin bound the envelope to the product — a self-hosted `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL` or a future Predge product in this envelope would have passed. `resource` is the signed field that makes that binding, and it is now checked.

**`pnpm check`.** Failed exactly as you quoted, for the reason you gave — `plugins/**` is excluded in `biome.jsonc`, so the sources passed and the one test file this PR adds did not. `pnpm fix` applied; `pnpm check` and `pnpm type-check` are both clean at head, and the unit suite passes.

## Mechanical

- **Example wallet.** It 404s today, confirmed. There is no stable answer available: `conviction` is a percentile within a set that gets re-ranked, so no address is permanently in it. Taking your second option — the address stays as an address-shaped example and a new `helpText` on the field says only verified smart-money wallets carry a signal, that the set is re-ranked so a wallet can leave it, and that the prefilled example may no longer be ranked. The comment above `example` says why, for the next person who wonders whether to go find a "better" one.
- **429.** Now `EXTERNAL` with its own message, ahead of the generic `< 500` branch. Same reasoning as `plugins/discord/steps/send-message.ts` and `plugins/pagerduty/steps/pagerduty-core.ts`: transient, and not the author's configuration.
- **Unparseable `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL`.** Checked before `assertUrlIsPublic`, so the `TypeError` never happens and the operator's typo is `USER` with the URL in the error, rather than Predge being blamed for a failed reach. Tested.
- **`TRAILING_SLASH_RE`.** Both copies gone, both call sites on `stripTrailingSlashes` from `lib/utils/url`. It is not on this branch's old base, which is part of why they were written locally; the rebase brought it.
- **Body size cap.** `content-length` checked before the body is read, body length before it is parsed, 64 KiB, mirroring `plugins/web3/steps/check-approval-exploit.ts`. `response.json()` is gone in favour of `text()` plus an explicit parse, so a non-JSON body is a clean failure instead of a thrown `SyntaxError`. Both cap paths and the parse failure are tested, including that `text()` is never called when the declared length is over.
- **`source?: string`.** Removed. The signal service does not emit it.
- **Non-200 branches.** All of them asserted now: 404, 402, 429, 5xx, an unexpected 4xx, non-JSON, oversized by header, oversized by body, SSRF, and the unparseable URL above. You were right that they failed closed; nothing held them to it.

## Docstrings

`index.ts:22` said a workflow only ever acts on a verified number and the action description said a successful step is a verified signal. Neither was true, as you said. Both now hold and both name the checks that make them hold, rather than being softened: the description lists the signature, the `resource` binding and the field checks, and says the conviction is always a number in 0-100. The `conviction`, `action`, `window`, `success` and `error` output descriptions say the same thing in their own terms, and `ReadSignalResult` in `read-signal.ts` carries `PredgeAction` and `PredgeWindow` instead of `string`.

## Housekeeping

Rebased onto `staging`; `pnpm discover-plugins` re-run afterwards with no diff in the generated files. The PR body is updated — it described the pre-shape-check behaviour and the five-check verifier.

Nothing here touches the allowlist question, which is yours and unchanged.

Three code items from the last round are in at `5fcd40b`.

**`verified` now documents six checks.** The `PredgeVerifyResult.verified` comment and the ordered list on `verifyPredgeSignal` both list the `resource` binding, in position, between subject binding and freshness. The docstring stays the source of truth for the word.

**`MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` comment reworded** to the caveat `plugins/web3/steps/check-approval-exploit.ts:68-79` already states: the cap bounds what is parsed, not what is allocated, because `response.text()` materialises a body that declared no `content-length` before its length can be read, and `body.length` counts UTF-16 code units rather than bytes. The declared-length check is named as the allocation bound for a server that states one. The 64 KiB behaviour is unchanged.

**Resource mismatch now routes through `blameForBadBody`.** You are right that it is the same mistake as a body that was never a Predge response, one layer in. Rather than matching a prefix literal in `read-signal.ts`, the reason's opening words are an exported `RESOURCE_MISMATCH_REASON` that the verifier builds the message from and the step classifies on, so a reworded message cannot silently change attribution. `blameForBadBody`'s docstring now lists it as the fifth depth. Covered both ways in the resource-binding suite: default host gives `EXTERNAL`, `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL` set gives `USER`. The suite is 42/42 and `biome check` is clean on the changed files.

**Screenshots** are the one item still open on my side. Config panel with the wallet `helpText`, the connection dialog with all three fields, and the Predge entry in the action picker, light and dark. Posting them here shortly.

**Pinned key:** understood, not writing either version. Standing by for the team's verdict. The offer to publish the next key id ahead of a cutover holds either way.

Screenshots, plus two things I found while taking them that you should know before you look at the images.

The Wallet input with `helpText` rendered as muted text underneath, which is the part you asked to see.

---

## The credential form is currently unreachable, and that is my bug

Shot 2 is an **Edit connection** form. I could not reach the create form by any click path, and I do not think anyone can.

`ConnectionTypePicker` (`components/overlays/add-connection-overlay.tsx:88-90`) lists only `getIntegrationTypes().filter(integrationRequiresCredentials)`, and `integrationRequiresCredentials` (`lib/integration-helpers.ts:13-22`) returns false for any plugin declaring `requiresCredentials: false` — which this plugin does, because every field is optional and the step works with none of them set. The node config panel gates its Connection block on the same flag (`components/workflow/config/action-config.tsx:1077-1079`).

So the three fields render correctly and are wired correctly, but nothing in the UI opens them. To capture shot 2 I created a `predge` integration row through `POST /api/integrations`, which made it appear under Connections; the Edit form reads `plugin.formFields` unconditionally and renders the same label/input/help markup the create form would. No source was changed to take any of these.

That matters beyond screenshots: `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` is the operator's escape hatch when we rotate the signing key, and right now an operator cannot set it without an API call. I did not want to guess your preference between the two obvious fixes, so I have not written either:

- have `integrationRequiresCredentials` also return true when a plugin declares `formFields`, regardless of `requiresCredentials`; or
- keep the flag as the gate for the picker, but let the node config panel show the Connection block whenever `formFields` is non-empty, so the fields are reachable from the node that uses them.

The first changes shared behaviour for every plugin, the second is local to this surface. Tell me which you want and I will send it, here or as a separate PR.

## There is no light theme to screenshot

`app/layout.tsx:149` sets `forcedTheme="dark"` on the ThemeProvider with no condition and no toggle anywhere in the UI. The light token set exists in `globals.css` but nothing reaches it.

To produce the light images I removed that one line locally, captured with Playwright's `colorScheme: 'light'` (next-themes then resolves to `html class="light"`, a real re-render rather than a filter), and reverted the file with `git checkout` before re-capturing the dark set from unmodified source. So the light images show how the plugin sits on the repo's light palette, but they are not a state a user of this build can currently reach. I would rather say that than let you assume the light shots are a normal mode.

My working tree is clean and nothing from any of this is on the PR branch.

reviews.body:
The egress side is right: `assertUrlIsPublic` runs before anything leaves, both paths go through `safeFetch`, and the base URL being configurable is handled rather than assumed.

The signature check does not establish what the plugin says it establishes.

## What this changes

Verification stops trusting the key the response carries. `verifySignedAttestation` is replaced by `verifyPredgeSignal`, which runs five ordered checks and returns a structured result: scheme, signer against a pinned key, ed25519 signature over the canonical payload, the payload's subject against the requested wallet, and `issuedAt` against a max-age window with a minute of skew tolerance. The pin defaults to a source constant (`predge-core.ts:34-35`) and `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` overrides it rather than being the only thing that enables pinning. `fetchSignedSignal` gains a 10s `AbortSignal.timeout` and a 402 branch. The step surfaces `reason`, `subjectMatch`, `issuedAt` and `ageSeconds`, a `PREDGE_MAX_SIGNAL_AGE_SECONDS` connection field carries the window, `canonicalize` becomes exported so tests can produce the verifier's exact bytes, and `tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts` drives the WebCrypto path across pass, wrong signer, tampered payload, wrong wallet, stale and future-dated.

## Does it match the description

Undersells. The body still says "Optional `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` pins a trusted signer; otherwise any key the signal carries is accepted", which is the behaviour this code removed, and its output list predates `reason`, `subjectMatch`, `issuedAt` and `ageSeconds`.

## Blocking

- The issue gate. `#2482` is filed, the reference in the body is right, and it carries `enhancement` and `needs-discussion`. It is not `accepted` because of an open question on our side, not anything missing on yours. There is nothing for you to do here, nothing to refile, and nothing to re-trigger. Clearing it is mine, and where it stands is in the team section below.

- `plugins/predge/steps/read-signal.ts:86-99` - a failed verification still returns `success: true` with the payload beside it. Nothing has been pushed since I raised this on `#2482`, so this is carried rather than attempted. `conviction`, `action` and `window` come straight from `signed.attestation.payload` whatever `verification.verified` says, and an author who gates a transfer on `conviction > 80` and forgets the second condition moves value on numbers nothing vouched for. Three more follow from the same line:
  - `:89` - `wallet: signal.wallet ?? wallet` emits the payload's subject, so a signal about a different wallet is reported under that wallet rather than the one asked for.
  - `:86` - `signed.attestation.payload` is dereferenced unconditionally after `verifyPredgeSignal` has already handled the malformed case. A host returning `200 {}` throws a TypeError out of the step, so `reason` is unreachable in exactly the case it was added for.
  - `predge-core.ts:192-199` - `fail()` fills `subjectMatch` and `issuedAt` on the paths that return before the signature is checked, so a signal minted with any keypair naming the requested wallet yields `subjectMatch: true`. `index.ts:104` calls that "the signed payload", which is unearned on those paths.

  Returning `{ success: false, error: verification.reason, errorClass: ExecutionErrorType.EXTERNAL }` when `verified` is false closes all four: a gate that did not hold belongs on the error path, not in the data. `tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts:241-255` asserts the current shape (`out.success` true beside `out.verified` false) and moves with it.

## Mechanical - actionable as-is

- `plugins/predge/steps/predge-core.ts:187-190` - `subjectMatch` runs `normalizeWallet` before the malformed guard at `:201`, and `:207` calls `signer.toLowerCase()`. A response carrying `payload.wallet` or `keyId` as a truthy non-string (`{"wallet": 123}` from a self-hosted `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL`) throws instead of returning the clean `verified: false` the docstring at `:164-167` promises. Compute `subjectMatch` after the guard and type-check both fields.
- `plugins/predge/steps/predge-core.ts:34-35` - `keyId` is compared against the 64-hex `public_key`, but the keyset names the 16-hex value `kid` and the attestation field is called `keyId`. If the live service puts the short form there, the pin fails on every real response and `verified` is permanently false with `reason: "signer is not the pinned Predge key"`, indistinguishable from an attack. Nothing establishes which form it emits: every positive test passes `expectedKeyId` from a generated keypair, so the constant is only ever exercised in rejection cases, and both sides of every signature test share the exported `canonicalize`, so a byte mismatch with your real signer is invisible too. A fixture captured from a live 200, asserted to verify against the default pin with no override, closes both. `tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts:63` declares a `keyId` override for exactly the "claims the pin, signs with another key" case and no test uses it.
- `lib/types/integration.ts:12` - the union member is hand-added but the generated header's `Generated types:` list still omits `predge`, so the committed file is not what `pnpm discover-plugins` emits and the next person to run it gets an unrelated-looking diff. Run it and commit the result.
- `plugins/predge/index.ts:109` - `ageSeconds` is documented as "-1 if unknown", but `predge-core.ts:230` tolerates `issuedAt` up to 60s ahead, so a fully verified signal issued a second in the future reports `-1`. Use a separate sentinel, or say the field can be negative. `:95` has the same kind of drift: it says "the pinned Predge key" when an override makes it the operator's key.
- `plugins/predge/steps/read-signal.ts:49-55` - `parseMaxAgeSeconds` falls back to 600 on anything it rejects, so an operator typing `0` into the new field intending "only brand new" silently gets the default with nothing in `reason`.
- The rotation path still is not written into the plugin. The day the pinned constant rotates, every default-configured workflow fails closed until a new constant ships from here, and only an operator who has set `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` can move first. A note next to that field in `credentials.ts` saying that is what it is for on a rotation covers it.
- The PR body's signer paragraph describes the superseded behaviour.
- Still open from my side, not blocking: a wallet that currently has a signal. `/v1/signal/` returns `{"error":"no_signal"}` with a 404 for every address I have tried, including just now, so I have still not seen a signed 200 to run against the pin. The keyset checks out and serves the constant at `predge-core.ts:34-35` with `role: "attestation"`, `active: true`.

## With the team

- Whether one party's signing key belongs in our tree as the root of trust for a gate we tell authors to hang value movement on. `plugins/plugin-allowlist.json` is one flat global list with no per-org or beta dimension, so it is on for everyone or no one, and allowlisting also puts that party's uptime on the execution path. The engineering is not what is holding this. I am weighing shipping against adding a scoping dimension to the allowlist first: the first accepts a dependency we cannot narrow later without a migration, the second is our work and delays this. I am taking it to the core team now and will come back with where it lands. Nothing about it is blocked on you.

## Verdict

Changes requested: a failed verification still returns `success: true` with the unverified payload beside it.

## What this changes

Two commits, both pushed after the PR was closed, so this increment has never been reviewed.

`plugins/predge/steps/read-signal.ts:93-99` returns `{ success: false, error: "Predge signal did not verify: <reason>", errorClass: EXTERNAL }` when verification fails, and the payload is dereferenced only after that check (`:101`). `:106` emits the requested address rather than the payload's. The success type drops `verified`, `reason` and `subjectMatch`. `predge-core.ts:197-210` adds a malformed guard that runtime-type-checks `signature`, `scheme`, `keyId` and `payload.wallet` through an `unknown` view before any string method touches them; `:223` hardcodes `subjectMatch: false` on failure and the real binding moves to after the signature check. `parseMaxAgeSeconds` now honours `0`. The tests add a captured live 200 asserted against `DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER` with no override, four malformed bodies, and a step-level malformed case.

## Does it match the description

Matches. Every substantive claim holds at head. Mildly undersold: the body does not mention the example-wallet change or the `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` typing fix.

## Previously raised

All of them are addressed: the `success: true` on failed verification, the wallet reported from the payload, the unconditional payload deref, `fail()` claiming `subjectMatch: true` before the signature check, malformed `keyId`/`wallet` throwing, the `keyId`-versus-`kid` question, the generated header in `lib/types/integration.ts`, the `ageSeconds` and signer wording, and the rotation path. `parseMaxAgeSeconds` is addressed in code but not in the help text - see below.

I did not take the fixture on trust. `DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER` (`predge-core.ts:34-35`) is byte-identical to the `attestation`-role active key published at `api.predge.io/.well-known/predge-keys.json` today.

You were also right about the 404s, and I was wrong. `0x1f9840...F984` is the UNI token contract, so it was never going to be a tracked wallet - that was a testing-address problem on my side, not an endpoint problem on yours. The replacement is an EOA and returns a live signed 200.

## Mechanical - actionable as-is

- `plugins/predge/steps/predge-core.ts:90-91,97-98` - the `PredgeVerifyResult` doc comments contradict the new code. `verified` is described as the field a workflow gates value movement on, but the step now fails instead and the field is no longer an output; `subjectMatch` is described as a wallet comparison while `:223` forces it `false` on every failure path. Reword both to match the inline note at `:217-218`.
- `plugins/predge/index.ts:62` - the max-age help text says only "Defaults to 600" and not that `0` is now honoured literally. An operator who types `0` meaning "strictest" gets `attestation is stale (0s old)` on every run, since any network latency exceeds it. One clause, or floor the value.
- `plugins/predge/steps/read-signal.ts:97` - `EXTERNAL` covers failures the operator caused, including a `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` typo and a malformed response from their own `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL`. Attribution only, no retry coupling, but `USER` is the right class for those two reasons.
- Rebase. The branch is `CONFLICTING` on three generated files because `staging` added `pagerduty` where this inserts `predge`. Re-run `pnpm discover-plugins` after rebasing rather than hand-editing.

`contracts-checked` was red for want of the label rather than anything in the diff - the one address in `index.ts` returns `0x` from `eth_getCode`, so it is an EOA, unlike the contract address it replaced. I have applied the label. `check-issue-link` is red on #2482, which is my triage queue, not yours.

## With the team

- Root of trust and allowlist scoping, carried and unchanged. There is a seam that lets the code land either way: `scripts/discover-plugins.ts` only emits an import for plugins listed in `plugins/plugin-allowlist.json`, while the `integration.ts` union covers every discovered plugin. So the plugin, its tests and the union member can land with the one-line allowlist entry withheld - in-tree and type-checked, registering nothing and rendering nothing. I'm settling the scoping question now and will come back shortly.
- The live fixture couples our CI to your key rotation: a legitimate rotation breaks the suite until someone captures a fresh 200, against relaxing it and leaving `DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER` as the one constant no test exercises against real bytes. I lean toward keeping it.

## Verdict

changes-requested on three doc and classification items plus the rebase - the blocking finding is genuinely closed, and I verified the pin against Predge's live published key rather than against the fixture alone.

## Blocking

**The signature verifies, the payload shape does not, so a verified signal can carry anything.**

`predge-core.ts:197-216` runtime type checks `scheme`, `keyId` and `payload.wallet`. `conviction`, `action` and `window` are read raw at `read-signal.ts:131-133` and returned typed as `number` and `string`.

Run against the real step with the real verifier and a correctly signed envelope:

```
conviction: "99999"        -> returned as the string "99999"
conviction: absent         -> success: true, and no conviction key in the output at all
action: {"evil":1}         -> returned as an object
conviction: -500           -> returned as is
```

A workflow gating on `{{@Predge.conviction}} >= 80` fires on the string case, because `"99999" >= 80` coerces true, on a value far outside the 0 to 100 range `index.ts:89` documents. The absent case is worse in the other direction: a `conviction < 30` branch silently never fires, and a template interpolating it into a trade size renders empty, with `success: true` throughout.

`index.ts:22` says a workflow only ever acts on a verified number, and `:80` says a successful step is a verified signal. Neither holds until the fields are checked.

**`resource` is signed but never read, so there is no domain separation between signed products.**

`resource` is declared on `PredgeAttestation` (`predge-core.ts:58`) and covered by the signature, and nothing validates it. The only thing distinguishing a conviction signal from another attestation of the same scheme is `payload.wallet`.

A wallet track record envelope signed by the same key, carrying `conviction_score` and a `verdict` rather than `conviction`, passes every check the plugin makes and produces the silent-success case above. Comparing `resource` against the expected `conviction:<wallet>` closes this and the absent-field case together.

**`pnpm check` fails on this branch.**

```
tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts:27:1   assist/source/organizeImports
tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts:164:38 lint/style/useNumericSeparators
tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts        format
Found 3 errors.
```

All three are in the one file this PR adds. `plugins/**` is excluded in `biome.jsonc`, which is why the plugin sources pass and the test file does not. `pnpm fix` resolves it. Worth noting the lint job has not run on this PR at all, so CI would not have told you.

## Mechanical

- `plugins/predge/index.ts:11-13` ships an example wallet with a comment saying it returns a live signed signal rather than a 404. It returns 404 today. The ranked set is transient, and `example` feeds AI workflow generation, so the generated default produces a step that fails on first run. Either pick a stable wallet or say in the help text that a wallet can leave the set.
- `predge-core.ts:318-325` maps every non-404, non-402 status under 500 to `ExecutionErrorType.USER`. A 429 from the default host is not the author's configuration, and there is no retry, so a scheduled workflow hitting a rate limit fails permanently into the customer's error budget. `plugins/discord/steps/send-message.ts:200` and `plugins/pagerduty/steps/pagerduty-core.ts:985` both treat 429 as transient.
- `predge-core.ts:344-348` special cases only `SsrfBlockedError`, so a malformed `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL` throws a plain `TypeError` from `assertUrlIsPublic` and is reported as `EXTERNAL`. That is an operator typo being attributed to Predge, which is the split `classifyVerificationFailure` at `read-signal.ts:70-83` exists to keep right.
- `predge-core.ts:24` and `test.ts:2` each add a fresh `const TRAILING_SLASH_RE = /\/+$/`. `lib/utils/url.ts` exports `stripTrailingSlashes` under a comment recording that this exact line had been declared eighteen times under three names in two flavours. `plugins/blockscout/test.ts`, the nearest sibling with the same client bundle constraint, imports the helper.
- `predge-core.ts:328` calls `response.json()` with no size cap on an operator chosen host. `plugins/web3/steps/check-approval-exploit.ts:267-276` caps both the declared `content-length` and the body.
- `predge-core.ts:53` declares `source?: string` on `PredgeConvictionSignal`, which nothing reads.
- Every non-200 branch of `fetchSignedSignal` is untested: all nine step tests mock `safeFetch` with `ok: true`. The 404, 402, generic non-ok, SSRF and JSON-parse paths do fail closed, they are simply unasserted.

## Verdict

changes-requested on the payload shape, `resource`, and the lint failure.

The crypto itself is real and checks out rather than being taken on trust: the pinned key matches the published keyset, and the committed fixture's signature verifies against it when the canonical bytes are rebuilt independently. `egress: "user-destination"` is the correct tier, the `safeFetch` and `assertUrlIsPublic` and `AbortSignal.timeout` triple is present on the step path, and the generated files are a true regeneration.

## What this changes

The branch was rebased, so I compared each file at `b957594` against `62edf7b` rather than reading a compare range. The registration files and `credentials.ts`/`icon.tsx` are unchanged. `verifyPredgeSignal` now requires `resource` to be a string (malformed otherwise) and, after subject binding, compares it against `conviction:<requested wallet>` (`predge-core.ts:287-291`). A new `parseConvictionPayload` (`predge-core.ts:348`) runs after verification in the step (`read-signal.ts:142-148`) and fails it unless `conviction` is a finite number in 0-100, `action` is one of accumulate/reduce/hold and `window` is 7d or 30d, with no coercion; the output type narrows to `PredgeAction`/`PredgeWindow`. `fetchSignedSignal` rejects an unparseable base URL as `USER` before `assertUrlIsPublic` (`:447-453`), files 429 as `EXTERNAL` (`:483-492`), refuses a body over 64 KiB by `content-length` and then by length, and replaces `response.json()` with `text()` plus a guarded `JSON.parse`. `blameForBadBody` centralises the "operator repointed the host" attribution. Both trailing-slash regexes are replaced by `stripTrailingSlashes`, `source?` is dropped, the wallet field gains `helpText`, the descriptions are rewritten, and the test file adds suites for payload shape, resource binding and every non-200 branch.

## Does it match the description

Matches. Every behavioural claim in the body holds at `62edf7b`: six ordered checks with `resource` fifth, the shape gate with no coercion, the 64 KiB cap checked by header and then by length, and the error attribution as listed.

## Blocking

- `#2482` is not labelled `accepted` yet, so `check-issue-link` is red. That one is mine to clear, not yours - the reference is right. Nothing to do on your side, and no need to refile.
- Payload shape - addressed. `parseConvictionPayload` (`predge-core.ts:348`) runs before success (`read-signal.ts:142-148`), and the four reproductions plus `conviction: 101`, `null`, `window: "90d"` and `action: "liquidate"` are tests against the real step (`tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts:487`).
- `resource` domain separation - addressed. `predge-core.ts:287-291` compares the signed `resource` to `conviction:<wallet>`, which matches the captured live fixture's format, and `tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts:612` covers both a foreign product and a foreign wallet.
- `pnpm check` on the test file - addressed per your report. I have not re-run it on this head.
- Operator-caused failures filed as `EXTERNAL` - addressed, and your version is better than what I asked for. Blaming the operator only when they set `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` or `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL` (`read-signal.ts:83-95`) is right, because on the defaults those failures are the upstream's. Keep it conditional; there is no need to flatten it.
- The `PredgeVerifyResult` doc comments (`predge-core.ts:119-134`), the max-age help text (`index.ts:70-71`) and the rebase are addressed. The branch is `MERGEABLE`.

## Mechanical - actionable as-is

- The example wallet, 429, unparseable URL, `TRAILING_SLASH_RE`, body cap, `source?` and untested non-200 branches are all addressed (`index.ts:17-20`, `predge-core.ts:483`, `:447`, `:11`/`test.ts:1`, `:505-523`, the type at `:73-80`, and `tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts:656`). Three small code items and the screenshots remain.
- `predge-core.ts:120-121` and `:207-213` - both still list five checks (scheme, signer, signature, subject, freshness), but `verified` now also requires the `resource` binding at `:287`. Add it to both lists so that the docstring stays the source of truth for what `verified` means.
- `predge-core.ts:44-46` - the comment says the cap bounds what the host "can make the step allocate". `response.text()` at `:515` buffers a body that sent no `content-length` in full before the `:516` check, so it bounds what is parsed, not what is allocated. `body.length` also counts UTF-16 units, not bytes. `plugins/web3/steps/check-approval-exploit.ts:68-79` states exactly this caveat. Reword the comment to match that caveat. The 64 KiB behaviour itself is fine.
- `read-signal.ts:83-95` - a `resource` mismatch (`attestation is for ...`) always falls through to `EXTERNAL`. But a payload that is not a conviction signal from a repointed host is `USER` via `blameForBadBody`, and `blameForBadBody`'s docstring (`predge-core.ts:402-409`) describes these as the same mistake. Route the resource-mismatch reason through `blameForBadBody` as well.
- Screenshots. This plugin adds screens that none of the earlier rounds asked to see: the Read Predge Signal node's config panel, where the Wallet input now renders your `helpText` as muted text below it; the Predge connection dialog with Predge Signal URL, Pinned Signer Key (optional) and Max Signal Age, seconds (optional); and the Predge entry with `icon.tsx` in the action picker. Please attach one screenshot of each, in the light and dark themes if convenient.

## With the team

- Whether a workflow value-gate may trust a pinned third-party ed25519 key as its root of trust, and whether the global allowlist needs a scoping dimension first. You offered two ways to go. The first keeps the default pin as a source constant: onboarding needs nothing, but our tree carries your key, and one rotation fails every default-configured gate at once. The second makes `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` required and drops `DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER`: the repo carries no third-party key material, at the cost of onboarding friction and a live fixture that then only proves the canonical bytes. Your offer to publish the next key ahead of each cutover is part of that same weighing. Please do not write either version yet. I'm discussing it with the core team now and will come back with a verdict shortly. It blocks merging, and nothing here is blocked on you.

## Verdict

Changes requested for two comment fixes, one attribution line and the screenshots. The payload-shape, `resource` and attribution gaps are closed and tested, and the merge also waits on the root-of-trust decision above.
